metaDescription: Commercial pressure washers compared by engine ladder, triplex pump, duty cycle and flow, from Honda GX200 to GX390 units and a quiet electric option.
expertTake: The Simpson PowerShot 4200 with a Honda GX390 is the best commercial all-rounder here, the Simpson Aluminum Series 3600 with a GX200 is the value pick for lighter commercial work, and the Tecoloy electric is the one to buy for indoor jobs. Skip the oversized-label budget units if you will run a machine for hours every day: duty cycle exposes them first.
introParagraphs: Commercial use changes what matters. A homeowner runs a washer for an hour; a contractor runs one for six, in the heat, with a surface cleaner pulling steady load. The difference shows up in engine class, pump construction, cooling and how easily every wear part can be replaced.

That is why the useful questions are different from residential ones. Is the pump a serviceable triplex, does the engine have reserve beyond the pump's demand and can a failed part be fixed on site rather than shipped away. This guide ranks machines on those points, and treats peak labels with caution.

products.name: Simpson PowerShot 4200 PSI Honda GX390 4.0 GPM
products.description:
The GX390 and a 4.0 GPM triplex pump are the standard working pair for professional washing, and Simpson delivers it with a 50-foot dual-braided hose and a welded steel frame. A 389cc commercial engine has enough reserve to turn the pump at 4200 PSI all day, which is what keeps it from overheating or surging under a surface cleaner load.

The triplex plunger pump is described as maintenance-free, meaning it needs no regular lubricant changes in normal use, while still being a pump class that technicians can service. Low-oil shutdown protects the engine if the crankcase level drops.

Compared with the Aluminum Series it shares the engine and flow class, so the choice is mainly frame and finish. Compared with the GX270 PowerShot it moves about 14 percent more water. Keep the engine oil fresh, clean the air filter often in dusty sites and winterize the pump.
products.bestFor: Contractors who run a washer most days and need a proven 4 GPM engine and pump.
pros: Honda GX390 has reserve for continuous duty
Welded steel frame is built for transport
cons: Heavy without a ramp or lift
No hose reel or accessories included

products.name: Simpson PowerShot 4000 PSI Honda GX270 3.5 GPM
products.description:
The GX270 sits between the GX200 and GX390 in the Honda commercial ladder, and Simpson uses it to drive a 3.5 GPM triplex pump at 4000 PSI. That is enough flow for most surface cleaners and enough pressure for stubborn stains, with a lighter and cheaper package than the GX390 machines.

The welded steel frame is powder-coated for outdoor storage, and the AAA triplex plunger pump is described as maintenance-free. For a landscaping or property-maintenance crew that cleans pavements weekly, it covers the job without the weight of the biggest engine.

It gives up half a gallon per minute against the 4200 PSI GX390 version, which adds up over a big lot. In return it costs less and is easier to lift. Standard upkeep applies: oil, air filter, fuel stabilizer and pump winterizing.
products.bestFor: Property crews who want Honda reliability and 3.5 GPM at a lower weight.
pros: Honda GX270 balances weight and reserve
cons: Less flow than the 4 GPM machines
Short hose compared with the Aluminum Series

products.name: Simpson Aluminum Series 3600 PSI Honda GX200 2.5 GPM
products.description:
The Aluminum Series 3600 uses the smaller 196cc Honda GX200 with a triplex plunger pump, aimed at lighter commercial use such as car washes, restaurant exteriors and small contractors. It delivers a useful 3600 PSI at 2.5 GPM, with a 35-foot non-marring hose.

The 2.5 GPM flow is the limiting number. It will clean quickly with a wand but struggles to drive a large surface cleaner as fast as a 4 GPM machine. If your work is mostly spot cleaning, vehicles and fixtures, that is not a problem.

The Honda engine and triplex pump are the reasons to choose it over cheaper generic machines. Parts are stocked and service is straightforward. Change the oil, clean the filter and winterize it as you would any triplex machine.
products.bestFor: Light commercial crews that want Honda and triplex quality at a lower price tier.
pros: Honda GX200 engine and triplex pump
cons: Less reserve for heavy continuous duty

products.name: Simpson PowerShot 4400 PSI CRX 420cc
products.description:
Simpson's CRX 420cc engine gives this PowerShot a larger displacement than the GX390 and a higher 4400 PSI rating at the same 4.0 GPM. The AAA industrial triplex pump is maintenance-free, and the welded frame is built for job-site abuse.

The extra 200 PSI over the GX390 version helps with dried-on mud, paint prep and rust, while the flow decides cleaning speed. The engine brand is the main compromise: Honda parts and service are more widely available than CRX.

If you buy on price and engine size, it competes well. If you buy on service network, the Honda units win.
products.bestFor: Crews that want extra pressure at 4.0 GPM and accept a non-Honda engine.
pros: 4400 PSI at 4.0 GPM for tough stains
cons: CRX engine has less service coverage than Honda

products.name: TechSweepPro 4400 PSI 4.5 GPM 420cc Key Start
products.description:
This machine claims 4400 PSI at up to 4.5 GPM from a 15 HP, 420cc engine. The engine is sized appropriately for those figures, which is more credible than 7 HP engines claiming 4 GPM, though the 4.5 GPM is a maximum, not a sustained rating.

The key start is a real convenience on a work site. At a much lower price tier than the Simpson units, it will do commercial-type cleaning but with unknown pump construction and a thin service network.

Treat it as a value gamble: if you need a 4 GPM machine for part-time commercial use and can handle your own repairs, it is attractive. For daily use, Honda and a known triplex pump are safer.
products.bestFor: Part-time commercial users who want 4 GPM class output at a low price tier.
pros: 15 HP engine is sized for 4 GPM work
Lowest price tier among high-flow gas units
cons: Max flow is a peak figure

products.name: TechSweepPro 4800 PSI 500cc 18 HP Hose Reel
products.description:
The biggest engine in this guide is the 500cc, 18 HP unit, which drives a claimed 4800 PSI at 4.0 GPM. The engine margin is generous for that flow, and a hose reel is built in, which speeds setup and teardown, and which extends hose life by avoiding kinks.

One-button key start removes the recoil pull from a heavy engine. The risk is the unknown: the pump's design and materials are not detailed, and an 18 HP engine at a low price tier suggests cost cutting somewhere else.

It is the most aggressive spec on paper, but it should be viewed as a high-risk, high-reward purchase. If your work is intermittent, the reel and large engine make it a convenient tool.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prize a hose reel and engine size over brand heritage.
pros: Large 18 HP engine with ample margin

products.name: Tecoloy 2200 PSI 3.2 GPM Commercial Electric Inverter
products.description:
Tecoloy takes a different path: a 3 HP permanent magnet motor with variable frequency control driving a horizontal triplex pump with ceramic plungers. Running near 65 decibels, it is much quieter than a gas engine, and it produces no exhaust.

That makes it a strong choice for indoor spaces, hospitals, parking structures and food service, where gas engines are prohibited. 2200 PSI at 3.2 GPM is a good match for degreasing and general cleaning, though it is lower pressure than the gas machines.

The constraint is the electrical supply and the pressure ceiling. For dried-on mud or paint stripping outside, a gas machine is stronger. For daily indoor cleaning, this is the quiet, low-fume option.
products.bestFor: Indoor commercial cleaning where exhaust and noise are not acceptable.
pros: About 65 dB, much quieter than gas
Ceramic plungers on a horizontal triplex pump
cons: Max flow figure is a peak

buyingCriteria.explanation: GX200, GX270 and GX390 are the common steps: roughly 196cc, 270cc and 389cc. The GX200 in the Aluminum Series 3600 drives 2.5 GPM, the GX270 in the PowerShot 4000 drives 3.5 GPM and the GX390 in the PowerShot 4200 drives 4.0 GPM. Match the engine to the flow you need and pay for no more.

A triplex plunger pump with ceramic or hardened plungers is the commercial standard and can be serviced. Budget machines like the TechSweepPro units do not detail pump design, which is a risk for daily use. Ask about pump warranty and parts.
A 15 to 20 inch surface cleaner needs 3.5 to 4 GPM to spin properly. The 2.5 GPM Aluminum Series 3600 cleans well with a wand but slowly with a cleaner. Match flow to your most common attachment.

A machine that runs six hours a day needs engine reserve and a pump that handles heat. Engines running near their limit, like a 7 HP unit claiming 4 GPM, wear quickly. Oversized engines, as in the 18 HP TechSweepPro, run cooler.
The Tecoloy runs near 65 dB with no exhaust, which is why it suits indoor sites. It is limited to 2200 PSI and needs a heavy supply. Choose electric only where gas is not allowed.
A Honda engine can be serviced by dealers everywhere, and Simpson pumps have a known parts network. Generic machines depend on the seller for parts. Weigh downtime cost, not just purchase price.

specDecoder.meaning: A family of commercial small engines. The number roughly tracks displacement and torque.
specDecoder.watchFor: GX200 on the 3600, GX270 on the 4000 and GX390 on the 4200.

specDecoder.meaning: A sealed or long-life triplex pump that needs no routine oil change. It is still serviceable if it wears.
specDecoder.watchFor: Simpson's AAA pumps are described this way.

specDecoder.meaning: A peak flow figure, not necessarily sustained. Rated flow is usually lower.
specDecoder.watchFor: TechSweepPro and Tecoloy quote max flow.

specDecoder.meaning: An inverter that adjusts motor speed for efficiency and quiet. It reduces noise and wear.
specDecoder.watchFor: Tecoloy uses it with a permanent magnet motor.

specDecoder.meaning: A sensor that stops the engine if oil is too low. It protects against catastrophic damage.
specDecoder.watchFor: Standard on the Simpson Honda models.

howWeEvaluated.title: Engine class and reserve
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared engines by displacement and brand, from the GX200 to GX390 and from the 420cc to the 500cc generic units. Reserve over the pump's demand earned the most credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pump construction
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored documented triplex pumps from Simpson and Tecoloy, and marked down machines that did not detail their pumps.

howWeEvaluated.title: Flow and attachments
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed GPM against typical commercial attachments, because a surface cleaner needs 3.5 to 4 GPM.

howWeEvaluated.title: Duty cycle fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each machine to a daily run time, from light commercial for the GX200 to heavy for the GX390 and 18 HP units.

howWeEvaluated.title: Service and noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at parts networks, hose and frame quality and noise, noting the Tecoloy's 65 dB. Owner feedback patterns on cheap commercial claims shaped the scoring.

rows: Honda GX200 at a lower tier
4.5 GPM max at a low tier

cards.label: Honda
cards.text: The Simpson 3600, 4000 and 4200 use GX200, GX270 and GX390 engines with broad dealer support and known reliability.

cards.label: Non-Honda
cards.text: The Simpson 4400 uses CRX, and the TechSweepPro units use generic engines. They offer more displacement per cost but thinner service networks.

howToChoose.note: Pick Honda if downtime costs you money, non-Honda if budget is the priority.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for electric drive, low noise and no exhaust. Gas engines produce carbon monoxide and should never run indoors.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Tecoloy 2200 PSI electric runs near 65 dB with no engine exhaust, making it the only practical indoor choice here.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if the washer earns money daily, which points to the Simpson PowerShot 4200 GX390 for its engine and pump.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if use is occasional. The Aluminum Series 3600 or TechSweepPro units cover lighter work at a lower price.

maintenance.why: Commercial duty heats oil quickly. Fresh oil protects bearings.
A clogged filter starves the engine and shortens its life.
Even sealed triplex pumps should be checked for leaks and oil level.
High-pressure hoses fail suddenly. Replace worn or kinked ones.
Frozen water cracks pump heads. Drain and use antifreeze.

faq.q: What makes a pressure washer commercial?
faq.a: Engine reserve, a serviceable triplex pump, 3.5 to 4 GPM flow and parts availability. Label alone does not make a machine commercial.

faq.q: Which Honda engine do I need?
faq.a: The GX200 suits 2.5 GPM work, the GX270 suits 3.5 GPM and the GX390 suits 4.0 GPM. Match the engine to your flow requirement.

faq.q: Can I trust a 4800 PSI label?
faq.a: Treat it as a peak rating until the pump and engine are documented. An 18 HP engine can support it, but pump design matters as well.

faq.q: Why choose electric for commercial work?
faq.a: No exhaust and about 65 dB noise make it suitable for indoor and sensitive sites. The tradeoff is lower pressure.

faq.q: How long do commercial washers last?
faq.a: With oil changes and winterizing, a Honda and triplex setup can last many years of daily use. Budget machines typically last fewer.

faq.q: Do I need a surface cleaner?
faq.a: For flat areas, yes. It saves hours and avoids stripes, and it needs 3.5 to 4 GPM to work at full speed.
